title: Spikes have no slope
summary: Below threshold the output is 0. Above it, 1. A step has no slope to learn from.

terms.definition: A function that is 0 below threshold and 1 above it. A spike, as a function of voltage, is this step.
Away from the threshold the step is flat, so the derivative is 0. There is no local slope that says how to change the voltage.

cards.text:
Below the threshold the output is 0.
Above it the output is 1.
There is no in-between.

lines: The slope you can measure is 0.

cards.text:
Learning needs a slope: if the water changes a little, does the output change?
A step says no, almost everywhere.

question.prompt: A neuron sitting below threshold gives a nonzero slope for learning.
question.why: The output is flat there. The slope is zero, so the usual lesson cannot move.
question.simpler: Only exactly at the threshold is the step not flat, and that single point is not a usable slope.

recall.question: Why can’t you learn through a literal spike the usual way?
recall.answer: The spike is a step. Its slope is zero almost everywhere.

deeper.note: Neftci, Mostafa, and Zenke open with this obstacle. Sections II and III separate the missing slope from the other training problems.

paper.title: Surrogate Gradient Learning in Spiking Neural Networks
paper.section: Sections II and III. The derivative of the spike is the wall.
